project.name: AI Desktop Assistant
project.description: Altron is an autonomous Windows desktop assistant: a headless Python orchestrator that drives a local Flask HUD in the browser, always-on voice control (wake word, faster-whisper STT, TTS), permission-gated desktop and file automation tools, and Telegram remote control with out-of-band approvals, backed by the Anthropic Claude Messages API.

nodes.name: app.py
nodes.summary: Legacy (deprecated) PySide6 application bootstrap that wires Settings, the SQLite Database, AIClient, AgentExecutor, OmniRoute and the tray/chat/settings windows into a Qt event loop; superseded by main.py plus the Flask HUD.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Config package barrel that re-exports the Settings class from src.config.settings.

nodes.name: ai_client.py
nodes.summary: Anthropic Claude Messages API client with an endpoint hard-coded to api.anthropic.com (audit S2); provides message dataclasses, connection status tracking, tool-use requests, cancellation and connection testing over urllib.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a concurrent.futures Future plus a cancel flag to make blocking urllib calls cancellable from UI threads.

nodes.name: database.py
nodes.summary: Deprecated compatibility shim exposing DatabaseService as a thin subclass of src.storage.db.Database.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Storage package barrel that re-exports the SQLite Database class.

nodes.name: db.py
nodes.summary: SQLite persistence layer defining settings, conversations, messages, tool_executions and permissions tables, with dataclass row models and CRUD methods for chat history, tool audit logs and per-tool permission modes.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Barrel for the legacy PySide6 UI package, re-exporting SystemTrayIcon, ChatWindow and SettingsWindow.

nodes.name: chat_window.py
nodes.summary: Legacy PySide6 'dynamic island' notch chat window that drives the AgentExecutor, renders message/step bubbles and permission cards, and integrates always-on voice, TTS and Telegram remote commands; deprecated in favor of the Flask radar HUD.

nodes.name: settings_window.py
nodes.summary: Legacy PySide6 settings dialog with tabs for the Claude gateway config, per-tool permission table, system options (Windows startup registry entry) and the tool audit log; deprecated alongside the Qt UI.

nodes.name: system_tray.py
nodes.summary: Legacy PySide6 system tray icon with a context menu emitting chat, settings, about and exit signals plus balloon notifications.

nodes.name: Application
nodes.summary: Legacy Qt application lifecycle object that initializes the database, AI client, agent executor, OmniRoute and windows, and handles tray menu signals for chat, settings, about and exit.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Legacy entry function that constructs Application, initializes it and runs the Qt event loop, returning the exit code.

nodes.name: ConnectionStatus
nodes.summary: Enum of AI API connection states: disconnected, connecting, connected and error.

nodes.name: Message
nodes.summary: Chat message dataclass with conversion to Anthropic API format and dict (de)serialization.

nodes.name: AIResponse
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding an AI response's content, success flag, error and raw payload.

nodes.name: AIClient
nodes.summary: Claude Messages API client with fixed Anthropic endpoint, model normalization, tool-use requests, cancellable chat/send_message calls and test_connection; base_url and provider are ignored.

nodes.name: DatabaseService
nodes.summary: Legacy wrapper subclassing Database with an unchanged constructor, kept for old imports.

nodes.name: Conversation
nodes.summary: Dataclass row model for a conversation with id, title and timestamps.

nodes.name: ChatMessage
nodes.summary: Dataclass row model for a stored chat message belonging to a conversation.

nodes.name: ToolExecution
nodes.summary: Dataclass row model for an audited tool execution with parameters, result, status and timing.

nodes.name: Database
nodes.summary: SQLite database wrapper that creates and migrates the schema and exposes CRUD for settings, conversations, messages, tool execution logs and tool permission modes.

nodes.name: AgentBridge
nodes.summary: QObject exposing Qt signals that marshal agent steps, permission requests, responses and errors from worker threads to the UI thread.

nodes.name: MessageBubble
nodes.summary: Qt widget rendering a single user or assistant chat bubble.

nodes.name: StepBubble
nodes.summary: Qt widget showing an agent execution step such as a tool call and its result.

nodes.name: PermissionCard
nodes.summary: Qt card asking the user to approve, allow for the session or reject a pending tool permission request.

nodes.name: ChatWindow
nodes.summary: Main legacy notch chat window: animated collapse/expand geometry, foreground-app polling, always-on voice and TTS handling, Telegram command intake, and agent execution with step, permission and response handling.

nodes.name: is_windows_startup_enabled
nodes.summary: Checks the HKCU Run registry key to see whether the assistant is set to launch at Windows startup.

nodes.name: set_windows_startup
nodes.summary: Adds or removes the assistant's HKCU Run registry entry to toggle launching at Windows startup.

nodes.name: SettingsWindow
nodes.summary: Legacy Qt settings dialog building gateway, permissions, system and audit tabs; loads and saves config, tests the Claude connection, and manages tool permissions and audit logs.

nodes.name: SystemTrayIcon
nodes.summary: QSystemTrayIcon wrapper that draws its icon, builds the context menu, emits user action signals and shows notifications.

nodes.name: main.py
nodes.summary: Official Altron entry point and orchestrator: sets up logging, HUD status, database, Claude client, agent executor and approval manager, then starts the Flask HUD server, voice listener and Telegram listener on plain threads and supervises them until shutdown.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses plain threading.Thread workers and closures over shared state (e.g. a one-element list as a mutable bridge reference) instead of Qt event loops.

nodes.name: log.py
nodes.summary: Central logging setup for Altron: a RedactingFormatter that strips bot tokens and sk-ant- keys, a rotating altron.log handler in the runtime directory, and get_logger/setup_logging/shutdown_logging helpers.
nodes.languageNotes: Regex-based secret redaction is applied at the Formatter level, so every handler inherits it.

nodes.name: paths.py
nodes.summary: Resolves the runtime data directory (~/.ai-desktop-assistant or ALTRON_DATA_DIR) and builds paths for runtime files there, keeping mutable state out of the OneDrive project folder.

nodes.name: settings.py
nodes.summary: Configuration layer: resolves and caches the .env file, implements get_config_value precedence (.env > process env > default), safely quotes and writes AI config back to .env, and exposes the Settings dataclass with default Claude models.
nodes.languageNotes: Caches parsed .env contents keyed on file mtime/size stamp with a lock; @property accessors on the dataclass reject non-Anthropic base URLs.

nodes.name: hud_status.py
nodes.summary: Thread-safe in-memory HUD state (assistant state, log ring, CPU/RAM metrics via psutil) that is atomically flushed to status.json in the runtime directory for the radar HUD.
nodes.languageNotes: Atomic file writes via a temp file plus os.replace under a module-level lock.

nodes.name: apply_ai_config
nodes.summary: Applies model and API key settings from a config dict to the live AIClient after a HUD config update.

nodes.name: make_approval_listener
nodes.summary: Builds the approval event listener that logs pending/resolved approvals to the HUD and forwards requests to the Telegram approval bridge.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Orchestrator body: initializes all services, wires command handlers for HUD, voice and Telegram input into the agent executor, starts worker threads and supervises them until interrupt.

nodes.name: redact_secrets
nodes.summary: Removes Telegram bot tokens, sk-ant- API keys and explicitly passed secrets from a string.

nodes.name: RedactingFormatter
nodes.summary: logging.Formatter subclass that runs every formatted record through redact_secrets.

nodes.name: get_logger
nodes.summary: Returns a namespaced logger for a module.

nodes.name: setup_logging
nodes.summary: Idempotently installs a rotating file handler (1 MB x 3) and optional console handler with redacting formatters, honoring ALTRON_LOG_LEVEL.

nodes.name: shutdown_logging
nodes.summary: Removes and closes the handlers installed by setup_logging.

nodes.name: get_runtime_dir
nodes.summary: Returns the runtime data directory, honoring ALTRON_DATA_DIR, and ensures it exists.

nodes.name: runtime_file
nodes.summary: Returns the path for a named runtime file in the data directory, migrating legacy copies when needed.

nodes.name: resolve_env_path
nodes.summary: Determines which .env file is authoritative for configuration.

nodes.name: read_env_vars
nodes.summary: Parses the .env file into a dict with a stamp-keyed cache.

nodes.name: get_config_value
nodes.summary: Returns the first non-empty value for the given keys using .env > process environment > default precedence.

nodes.name: get_active_config_dict
nodes.summary: Builds the current effective AI configuration (model, masked key, language) for the HUD.

nodes.name: _format_env_value
nodes.summary: Quotes and escapes a value for safe writing to .env, rejecting line breaks.

nodes.name: load_env_file
nodes.summary: Loads the .env file into the process environment via python-dotenv.

nodes.name: is_masked_key
nodes.summary: Detects whether an API key value is the masked placeholder sent back by the HUD.

nodes.name: save_ai_config
nodes.summary: Validates and writes model, API key and language into the .env file, preserving other lines and raising on write failure.

nodes.name: Settings
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding application settings (data dir, db path, models, Telegram config) resolved through get_config_value, rejecting non-Anthropic base URLs/providers.

nodes.name: get_system_metrics
nodes.summary: Collects CPU, RAM and related system metrics via psutil for the HUD.

nodes.name: _flush_locked
nodes.summary: Atomically writes the in-memory HUD state to status.json while the lock is held.

nodes.name: get_hud_status
nodes.summary: Returns a snapshot of the current HUD status with fresh system metrics.

nodes.name: update_hud_status
nodes.summary: Updates the assistant state and/or appends a log entry, then flushes to disk.

nodes.name: clear_hud_logs
nodes.summary: Clears the HUD log ring and flushes.

nodes.name: init_hud_status
nodes.summary: Resets HUD state at startup and writes the initial status.json.

nodes.name: signals.py
nodes.summary: Qt-free CallbackSignal descriptor providing per-instance connect/disconnect/emit callback lists, letting listener classes mimic Qt signals without PySide6.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the descriptor protocol (__set_name__/__get__) to lazily bind a per-instance callback list, similar to Qt's bound signals.

nodes.name: telegram_service.py
nodes.summary: Telegram integration: message chunking and send helpers (text, documents, photos), a minimal Bot API client, the inline-keyboard TelegramApprovalBridge for out-of-band approvals, persisted update offsets, and the long-polling TelegramRemoteListener plus its legacy QThread wrapper.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses urllib only (no third-party Telegram SDK) with long polling; credentials are redacted from errors via redact_secrets.

nodes.name: voice_service.py
nodes.summary: Voice stack: text cleanup and wake-word parsing, TTSManager (edge-tts / Piper playback with mute and stop), energy- and webrtc-style VAD helpers, the always-on SpeechRecognitionListener using faster-whisper STT, and a legacy QThread wrapper.
nodes.languageNotes: Mixes asyncio (edge-tts), subprocess playback and numpy audio buffers; CallbackSignal descriptors replace Qt signals on the runtime path.

nodes.name: ui_server.py
nodes.summary: Flask HUD server on 127.0.0.1:5000 (fallback 5001) serving the ui/ assets and the JSON API (/status, /config, /test_config, /command, /clear_logs, /approvals, /approve), enforcing per-launch token auth, Host/Origin checks, JSON-only state changes and security headers.
nodes.languageNotes: A before_request hook centralizes auth (hmac.compare_digest on X-HUD-Token) and Host/Origin validation; the server runs in a daemon thread.

nodes.name: _BoundCallbacks
nodes.summary: Per-instance, thread-safe list of callbacks with connect, disconnect and emit that logs callback failures.

nodes.name: CallbackSignal
nodes.summary: Descriptor that gives each owner instance its own _BoundCallbacks, a Qt-free stand-in for Qt Signal.

nodes.name: chunk_message
nodes.summary: Splits long text into Telegram-sized chunks, preferring newline and space boundaries.

nodes.name: resolve_credentials
nodes.summary: Resolves the bot token and chat id from arguments or configuration.

nodes.name: send_telegram_message
nodes.summary: Sends a (chunked) text message through the Bot API, redacting the token from errors.

nodes.name: send_telegram_message_async
nodes.summary: Sends a Telegram message on a background thread.

nodes.name: _post_file
nodes.summary: Uploads a file to a Bot API method as multipart/form-data with size limits.

nodes.name: send_telegram_document
nodes.summary: Sends a document file to the configured chat.

nodes.name: send_telegram_photo
nodes.summary: Sends a photo to the configured chat.

nodes.name: send_telegram_photo_async
nodes.summary: Sends a photo on a background thread and logs failures.

nodes.name: TelegramBotApi
nodes.summary: Minimal JSON Bot API client wrapping urllib calls for a given token.

nodes.name: TelegramApprovalBridge
nodes.summary: Sends approval requests as inline-keyboard messages and resolves callback queries against the ApprovalManager, accepting only the owner chat and user.

nodes.name: load_update_offset
nodes.summary: Reads the persisted getUpdates offset for the current bot from the runtime directory.

nodes.name: save_update_offset
nodes.summary: Persists the getUpdates offset for the current bot atomically.

nodes.name: TelegramRemoteListener
nodes.summary: Qt-free long-polling listener that receives owner commands and callback queries, dispatching them via CallbackSignal and the approval bridge; the runtime path.

nodes.name: TelegramRemoteWorker
nodes.summary: Legacy QThread wrapper around TelegramRemoteListener kept for the deprecated PySide6 UI.

nodes.name: clean_text_for_speech
nodes.summary: Strips markdown, code, URLs and symbols from text so it reads naturally aloud.

nodes.name: parse_wake_word
nodes.summary: Detects the Altron wake word in transcribed text and returns the remaining command.

nodes.name: TTSManager
nodes.summary: Text-to-speech manager using edge-tts with Piper fallback, a worker queue, mute/enable controls, stop support and HUD state updates.

nodes.name: EnergyVAD
nodes.summary: Simple RMS-energy voice activity detector used as a fallback.

nodes.name: FastVAD
nodes.summary: Voice activity detector wrapper preferring a fast VAD backend with energy fallback.

nodes.name: SpeechRecognitionListener
nodes.summary: Qt-free always-on listener: captures microphone audio, gates with VAD, transcribes with faster-whisper, handles wake words and pause/abort, and emits recognized text via CallbackSignal; the runtime path.

nodes.name: SpeechRecognitionWorker
nodes.summary: Legacy QThread wrapper around SpeechRecognitionListener for the deprecated PySide6 UI.

nodes.name: set_approval_manager
nodes.summary: Registers the ApprovalManager used by the approval endpoints.

nodes.name: set_command_handler
nodes.summary: Registers the callback that executes commands posted from the HUD.

nodes.name: _get_default_browser
nodes.summary: Reads the Windows registry to find the default browser ProgID and executable.

nodes.name: open_hud_window
nodes.summary: Opens the HUD URL in an app-style Chromium window when available, else the default browser, without shell=True.

nodes.name: _enforce_hud_security
nodes.summary: before_request hook enforcing Host/Origin checks, the X-HUD-Token constant-time comparison and JSON content type for state-changing requests.

nodes.name: _validate_config_payload
nodes.summary: Validates /config payloads, rejecting base_url/provider keys and values containing line breaks.

nodes.name: index
nodes.summary: Serves index.html with the per-launch HUD token injected.

nodes.name: config_route
nodes.summary: GET returns the active AI config; POST validates and saves model/key/language and notifies the orchestrator.

nodes.name: test_config_route
nodes.summary: Tests connectivity to the Claude API with the configured key and model.

nodes.name: command_route
nodes.summary: Accepts a command from the HUD and dispatches it to the registered command handler.

nodes.name: approve_route
nodes.summary: Resolves a pending approval by id and args hash from the authenticated HUD.

nodes.name: start_hud_server
nodes.summary: Starts the Flask app on a daemon thread on port 5000 (falling back to 5001), wiring handlers and optionally opening the HUD window.

nodes.name: memory.py
nodes.summary: Backward-compatibility shim at the project root that only re-exports ConversationMemory from src.agent.memory so legacy imports keep working.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package barrel for the agent layer, re-exporting the tool registry, AgentExecutor and its data types, PermissionGate/PermissionLevel and ConversationMemory.

nodes.name: approvals.py
nodes.summary: Out-of-band approval flow (audit S5): a thread-safe, non-blocking ApprovalManager whose requests use unguessable ids, are bound to a SHA-256 hash of tool name plus args, expire after a TTL, are single-use, and can only be resolved by allowed channels (never voice).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses dataclasses, hmac.compare_digest for constant-time hash checks, and injectable clock/dispatch callables to keep the manager deterministic in tests.

nodes.name: executor.py
nodes.summary: Core agent loop: AgentExecutor sends conversation plus tool schemas to Claude via AIClient, parses tool_use blocks, routes each call through the permission gate and ApprovalManager, and post-processes replies; also hosts local intent matching and reply-sanitizing helpers.
nodes.languageNotes: Very large module mixing regex-heavy heuristic helpers (local intent matching, payload interception) with a stateful executor class driven by an Enum state machine.

nodes.name: args_hash
nodes.summary: Computes a canonical SHA-256 of tool name and args with sorted keys so an approval is bound to the exact arguments.

nodes.name: summarize_args
nodes.summary: Produces a truncated single-string JSON preview of tool args for display in approval prompts.

nodes.name: ApprovalRequest
nodes.summary: Dataclass for one pending approval: id, tool, args, args hash, origin channel, expiry, allowed approver channels and status, with a public_view for the HUD/Telegram.

nodes.name: ResolveResult
nodes.summary: Dataclass wrapping the outcome of resolving a request, with an ok property true only for approved or denied.

nodes.name: ApprovalManager
nodes.summary: Thread-safe registry that creates, lists, sweeps and resolves approval requests, checks channel and hash, enforces single use and expiry, notifies listeners, and runs the stored args exactly once on a dispatch worker.

nodes.name: AgentState
nodes.summary: Enum of executor states: idle, thinking, awaiting_permission, executing, complete and error.

nodes.name: AgentStep
nodes.summary: Dataclass recording one step of the agent loop such as a tool call and its result.

nodes.name: AgentResponse
nodes.summary: Dataclass carrying the final assistant reply plus the steps taken and any pending permission.

nodes.name: PermissionRequest
nodes.summary: Legacy in-process permission prompt object with an event the desktop chat window approves, rejects or session-allows while the loop waits.

nodes.name: match_local_intent
nodes.summary: Large heuristic matcher that maps common user prompts (English and Arabic) directly to a tool call, bypassing the model for fast local actions.

nodes.name: clean_tool_confirmation
nodes.summary: Builds a clean human-readable confirmation message from a tool name, its input and result instead of leaking raw output.

nodes.name: intercept_raw_code_or_payload
nodes.summary: Detects when the model replies with raw code or a JSON tool payload instead of a proper tool_use and converts it into an executed tool call with a clean confirmation.

nodes.name: sanitize_final_reply
nodes.summary: Strips leaked code, JSON payloads and internal markup from the final assistant reply before it reaches the user.

nodes.name: AgentExecutor
nodes.summary: Main agent loop class: builds Claude messages with tool schemas, parses tool_use, executes tools through PermissionGate tiers and the out-of-band ApprovalManager (passing approval only as approved=), records history in memory and the database, and updates HUD status.

nodes.name: memory.py
nodes.summary: Thread-safe JSON-backed conversation memory that persists recent messages to memory.json in the runtime directory and formats them for prompts.

nodes.name: permissions.py
nodes.summary: Permission gate (audit S4) classifying tools into SAFE, CONDITIONAL and DANGEROUS tiers, refusing blanket allows for conditional tools, plus per-call checks for sensitive paths, risky file extensions and non-plain app names.
nodes.languageNotes: Path checks canonicalize with realpath/expandvars and strip NTFS alternate-data-stream suffixes and trailing dots to defeat Windows path tricks.

nodes.name: tools.py
nodes.summary: Tool registry and all desktop automation handlers (files, terminal, apps, windows, web fetch with SSRF guard, system controls, YouTube, PDF, Telegram, screenshots, clipboard, WhatsApp); Tool.run strips every _-prefixed model input key so approval only arrives via the approved= kwarg (audit S3).
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy use of lazy imports (psutil, win32gui, ctypes, yt_dlp) so optional Windows-only dependencies load only when a tool runs; custom urllib handlers pin connections to public IPs to block SSRF and DNS rebinding.

nodes.name: ConversationMemory
nodes.summary: Thread-safe store that reads and writes recent conversation messages to a JSON file (default runtime memory.json), with helpers to add, fetch, format for prompts and clear.

nodes.name: PermissionLevel
nodes.summary: Enum of permission decisions: ask, allow (session) and deny.

nodes.name: PermissionRule
nodes.summary: Dataclass pairing a tool name with a PermissionLevel and optional conditions.

nodes.name: PermissionGate
nodes.summary: Classifies tools into SAFE, CONDITIONAL and DANGEROUS sets, tracks session rules (refusing blanket allow for conditional tools) and produces human-readable permission messages.

nodes.name: is_sensitive_path
nodes.summary: Returns true if a path resolves to a secret or credential location such as .env, private keys, .ssh/.aws or browser profile data.

nodes.name: needs_approval_file_read
nodes.summary: Per-call check for the conditional file_read tool: requires approval for sensitive paths.

nodes.name: needs_approval_file_open
nodes.summary: Per-call check for file_open: launchable or scriptable extensions need approval, documents auto-open.

nodes.name: needs_approval_app_open
nodes.summary: Per-call check for app_open: only plain app names or ms-settings URIs auto-open; paths, metacharacters and risky extensions need approval.

nodes.name: ToolCategory
nodes.summary: Enum grouping tools by category: file_system, terminal, system, browser, coding and utility.

nodes.name: ToolParameter
nodes.summary: Dataclass describing one tool input parameter: name, type, description, required flag, enum and default.

nodes.name: ToolResult
nodes.summary: Dataclass for a tool execution outcome (success, output, error, permission flags, message), copying message into dict output after init.

nodes.name: Tool
nodes.summary: Registered tool definition; run() strips _-prefixed model keys and passes approval only via the approved= kwarg (S3), and to_api_schema() emits the Anthropic tool schema.

nodes.name: strip_internal_keys
nodes.summary: Removes reserved _-prefixed keys from model-supplied tool input so the model cannot forge approval flags.

nodes.name: ToolRegistry
nodes.summary: Registry that stores tools by name, lists them by category, emits the tools schema for Claude and executes a tool by name.

nodes.name: handle_file_search
nodes.summary: Searches the filesystem for files matching a pattern under a directory.

nodes.name: handle_file_read
nodes.summary: Reads a text file; sensitive paths require approval via needs_approval_file_read.

nodes.name: handle_file_write
nodes.summary: Writes content to a file (dangerous tier, requires permission).

nodes.name: handle_file_delete
nodes.summary: Deletes a file or directory (dangerous tier, requires permission).

nodes.name: handle_file_copy
nodes.summary: Copies a file or directory, possibly overwriting (dangerous tier).

nodes.name: handle_file_move
nodes.summary: Moves or renames a file or directory (dangerous tier).

nodes.name: handle_file_open
nodes.summary: Opens a file with its default Windows application; executable types need approval.

nodes.name: handle_terminal_command
nodes.summary: Runs a PowerShell or cmd command by passing an argument list to subprocess.run with a timeout (dangerous tier, requires permission).

nodes.name: handle_app_open
nodes.summary: Launches an application non-blockingly; only plain app names auto-run, others need approval.

nodes.name: handle_app_close
nodes.summary: Closes an application by name via psutil (dangerous tier).

nodes.name: handle_browser_open
nodes.summary: Opens a URL or search in the browser without blocking.

nodes.name: handle_process_list
nodes.summary: Lists running processes with psutil.

nodes.name: handle_system_info
nodes.summary: Reports CPU, memory and OS information.

nodes.name: handle_window_control
nodes.summary: Lists, focuses, minimizes or maximizes windows through Win32 APIs via ctypes.

nodes.name: find_matching_window
nodes.summary: Fuzzy-matches a window query (including process names and Arabic aliases) to a top-level window handle using win32gui and difflib.

nodes.name: handle_move_application_window
nodes.summary: Moves, snaps, maximizes or minimizes an application window on screen.

nodes.name: handle_desktop_icon_position
nodes.summary: Repositions a desktop icon by delegating to desktop_icon_service.

nodes.name: handle_code_edit
nodes.summary: Performs a targeted search-and-replace inside a file (dangerous tier).

nodes.name: _resolve_public
nodes.summary: Resolves a host and rejects it unless every address is a public IP (SSRF guard).

nodes.name: _connect_public
nodes.summary: Opens a socket only to pre-validated public addresses, preventing DNS-rebinding SSRF.

nodes.name: handle_web_fetch
nodes.summary: Fetches a URL through the public-IP-pinned opener with redirect checks and extracts readable text.

nodes.name: handle_system_control
nodes.summary: Instant Windows controls for volume, brightness, lock and settings pages.

nodes.name: handle_youtube_play
nodes.summary: Searches YouTube and plays the first matching video in the browser.

nodes.name: extract_youtube_video_id
nodes.summary: Extracts an 11-character video id from a YouTube URL or raw id string.

nodes.name: fetch_youtube_transcript_text
nodes.summary: Fetches a video transcript via youtube_transcript_api with language fallbacks.

nodes.name: handle_youtube_play_and_summarize
nodes.summary: Finds or opens a YouTube video, optionally plays it, and fetches its transcript for summarization.

nodes.name: handle_create_and_send_pdf
nodes.summary: Generates a styled Arabic/English PDF on the Desktop and sends it to Telegram.

nodes.name: handle_send_to_telegram
nodes.summary: Sends text (auto) or local files (requires approval) to the authorized Telegram chat.

nodes.name: handle_capture_and_inspect_screen
nodes.summary: Captures a desktop screenshot, inspects open windows and sends the image to Telegram.

nodes.name: _record_clipboard_history
nodes.summary: Records clipboard text at the front of an in-memory history, deduplicated and capped at 20 items.

nodes.name: _get_clipboard_unicode
nodes.summary: Reads Unicode text from the Windows clipboard via ctypes.

nodes.name: _set_clipboard_unicode
nodes.summary: Writes Unicode text to the Windows clipboard via ctypes.

nodes.name: _simulate_keybd
nodes.summary: Simulates a key press (optionally with Ctrl) via keybd_event.

nodes.name: handle_clipboard_manager
nodes.summary: Clipboard tool: read, write, paste, copy selection, history and clear.

nodes.name: _mouse_click
nodes.summary: Moves the cursor and sends a left click via Win32 mouse events.

nodes.name: _focus_whatsapp_window
nodes.summary: Finds, restores and focuses the WhatsApp Desktop window, returning its rectangle.

nodes.name: _find_contact_element_uia
nodes.summary: Locates a WhatsApp contact list element through UI Automation and returns its center point.

nodes.name: _open_whatsapp_chat
nodes.summary: Opens a WhatsApp chat for a contact using UIA lookup, search-box typing and clipboard paste fallbacks.

nodes.name: handle_whatsapp_send
nodes.summary: Sends a WhatsApp Desktop message to a phone number or contact via deep links or UI automation.

nodes.name: handle_whatsapp_read
nodes.summary: Reads latest WhatsApp Desktop messages via UIA with Windows OCR fallback and delivers clean text to Telegram.

nodes.name: create_default_registry
nodes.summary: Builds the default ToolRegistry, registering every tool with its parameters, handler and permission flags.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Barrel for the src.services package that re-exports the Claude AI client, database service, OmniRoute manager, voice (TTS/STT listener) helpers, desktop icon helpers and Telegram send/listener APIs under a single __all__.
nodes.languageNotes: Python package barrel: importing src.services eagerly imports every service module, including Win32 ctypes and voice dependencies.

nodes.name: desktop_icon_service.py
nodes.summary: Win32 ctypes service that locates Explorer's desktop SysListView32, reads icon names and positions through cross-process memory, and moves desktop icons to preset or explicit screen coordinates. Backs the desktop_icon_position agent tool.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses VirtualAllocEx/ReadProcessMemory/WriteProcessMemory to marshal LVITEMW and POINT structures into explorer.exe, because list-view messages with pointers cannot cross process boundaries.

nodes.name: LVITEMW
nodes.summary: ctypes Structure mirroring the Win32 LVITEMW list-view item record, used to request icon text from the desktop list view.

nodes.name: get_desktop_listview_hwnd
nodes.summary: Finds the desktop SysListView32 window handle via Progman/SHELLDLL_DefView, falling back to enumerating WorkerW windows; returns None off Windows.

nodes.name: get_screen_dimensions
nodes.summary: Returns the primary screen width and height from GetSystemMetrics, with a default fallback on non-Windows systems.

nodes.name: get_desktop_icons
nodes.summary: Enumerates all desktop icons with name, list-view index and current position by allocating memory inside Explorer's process and sending LVM_GETITEMTEXTW/LVM_GETITEMPOSITION.

nodes.name: calculate_screen_coordinates
nodes.summary: Maps a preset position name (center, top, bottom_left, and so on) plus an offset index to concrete pixel coordinates, so multiple moved icons do not overlap.

nodes.name: position_desktop_icon
nodes.summary: Main entry point: resolves the target icon(s) by exact, substring or difflib fuzzy name match (or 'all'), computes destination coordinates, and moves them with LVM_SETITEMPOSITION, returning a structured success/error dict.

nodes.name: omniroute_manager.py
nodes.summary: Lifecycle manager for a local OmniRoute proxy on localhost:20128 that probes /v1/models, spawns the omniroute launcher without a shell if it is down, and terminates it only if it spawned it. Effectively dead code now: main.py only starts it when settings.ai_base_url contains '20128' or 'localhost', but ai_base_url is pinned to api.anthropic.com (S2), so the condition never holds.

nodes.name: OmniRouteManager
nodes.summary: Starts, health-checks and stops the OmniRoute proxy subprocess (resolved with shutil.which, CREATE_NO_WINDOW, polling up to 8 s) and tracks whether this instance owns the process. Still exported and instantiated by main.py, but unreachable under the Claude-only endpoint.

nodes.name: .env.example
nodes.summary: Committed environment template with placeholders for the Anthropic API key and the Telegram bot token and owner chat ID. The endpoint is fixed to api.anthropic.com and the model defaults in settings.py, so neither is set here.

nodes.name: CLAUDE.md
nodes.summary: Contributor and agent guide describing Altron's official runtime path (main.py + Flask HUD), module layout, configuration precedence, runtime directory, logging rules, security invariants S1-S8 and test conventions.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Bilingual (English/Arabic) project README covering Altron's capabilities, architecture table, runtime directory, security design, mandatory Telegram bot setup, installation steps, launch via python main.py and running tests.

nodes.name: pytest.ini
nodes.summary: Pytest configuration restricting collection to tests/ and test_agent.py (excluding legacy manual GUI scripts) and disabling the cache provider so no .pytest_cache lands in the OneDrive folder.

nodes.name: requirements.txt
nodes.summary: Python dependency list covering Flask HUD, voice stack (SpeechRecognition, PyAudio, sounddevice, faster-whisper, webrtcvad, edge-tts, pyttsx3), desktop automation (pywin32, comtypes, pyautogui, psutil), media tools and the legacy PySide6 UI.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses PEP 508 environment markers to pick webrtcvad-wheels on Windows and webrtcvad elsewhere, and to restrict pywin32/comtypes to win32.

nodes.name: .gitattributes
nodes.summary: Git attributes file normalizing line endings for all text files via `* text=auto`.

nodes.name: build_exe.py
nodes.summary: PyInstaller packaging script that bundles the official main.py orchestrator plus the Flask HUD (ui_server.py and ui/ assets) into a Windows console executable, with curated hidden imports, collect-all rules and excludes.
nodes.languageNotes: Drives PyInstaller programmatically via PyInstaller.__main__.run with an argument list instead of a .spec file.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Validates the main.py entry point and required HUD assets (index.html, app.js, style.css), then runs PyInstaller in onedir or onefile mode and reports success.

nodes.name: system_prompt.txt
nodes.summary: System prompt defining Altron's persona as a polite British-butler assistant, with a critical rule that replies are spoken by the built-in TTSManager rather than via terminal or PowerShell speech.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker for the top-level src package, containing only a docstring.

nodes.name: app.js
nodes.summary: HUD client script that polls /status and /approvals every second, renders system metrics, conversation logs and pending approvals, and drives command submission, settings and connection tests; every request carries the per-launch X-HUD-Token read from a meta tag.
nodes.languageNotes: All logic is wrapped in a strict-mode IIFE, so no globals leak and no functions are exported; escapeHtml guards innerHTML rendering of log content.

nodes.name: updateClockAndGreeting
nodes.summary: Updates the HUD clock, date and time-of-day greeting every second.

nodes.name: fetchStatus
nodes.summary: Polls /status with the X-HUD-Token header and dispatches state, metrics and logs to the render functions.

nodes.name: renderState
nodes.summary: Maps the assistant core state (listening, thinking, speaking, etc.) to the status indicator text and styling.

nodes.name: renderMetrics
nodes.summary: Renders CPU, temperature, RAM, disk and battery values and progress bars from status metrics.

nodes.name: renderLogs
nodes.summary: Renders conversation log entries as escaped chat bubbles and updates the events counter.

nodes.name: openSettingsModal
nodes.summary: Fetches current configuration from /config and opens the settings modal populated with model and language.

nodes.name: renderApprovals
nodes.summary: Renders pending tool-approval requests as cards with approve/deny buttons, toggling the approvals panel.

nodes.name: fetchApprovals
nodes.summary: Polls /approvals with the HUD token and renders pending approval requests.

nodes.name: submitApproval
nodes.summary: POSTs an approve/deny decision for a request to /approve as JSON with the HUD token.

nodes.name: index.html
nodes.summary: HUD page markup with clock, system stats, AI config card, command bar, approvals panel, chat feed and settings modal; carries the __HUD_TOKEN__ meta placeholder that ui_server.py replaces per launch.

nodes.name: style.css
nodes.summary: Sci-fi radar HUD stylesheet defining cyan-glow design tokens, card layouts, progress bars, chat bubbles, approvals cards, settings modal and animations.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the bilingual README, which presents Altron as an autonomous Windows desktop assistant and includes an architecture table, the runtime directory, the security design and the Telegram setup. CLAUDE.md is the contributor guide. It names main.py plus the Flask HUD as the only official runtime path, describes the module layout and configuration precedence, and lists the S1-S8 security invariants that the rest of this tour comes back to.

tour.title: The Orchestrator Entry Point
tour.description: main.py is the official entry point and has the highest code fan-out in the project. It sets up logging, HUD status, the database, the Claude client, the agent executor and the approval manager. It then starts the HUD server, the voice listener and the Telegram listener on plain Python threads and supervises them. Each direct import of main.py becomes a later stop on this tour, so treat this file as the map.
tour.languageLesson: Python's threading.Thread runs a target callable in a background OS thread. Setting daemon=True lets the process exit without waiting for it. A supervising main thread can call join() with a timeout or poll is_alive() to watch long-running workers.

tour.title: Configuration, Paths and Logging
tour.description: settings.py has the highest fan-in of any file because nearly every module reads configuration through get_config_value. That function applies one precedence rule: .env first, then the process environment, then the default. paths.py keeps mutable state in ~/.ai-desktop-assistant (or ALTRON_DATA_DIR) and out of the OneDrive-synced project folder. log.py adds a RedactingFormatter that strips bot tokens and sk-ant- keys before anything is written to the rotating altron.log. The committed .env.example is a template that lists the expected Anthropic and Telegram settings.
tour.languageLesson: A logging.Formatter subclass can override format() to post-process every record. Because it runs on each handler, it is a single place to redact secrets in all log output.

tour.title: Talking to Claude
tour.description: ai_client.py is the only path to a language model. It is a Claude Messages API client whose endpoint is hard-coded to api.anthropic.com (audit S2), and it provides message dataclasses and connection-status tracking. The system prompt gives Altron its polite British-butler persona and asks for replies that read well aloud, because the TTS engine you will meet in the voice step speaks them.

tour.title: The Agent Loop
tour.description: Using the AI client from Step 4, AgentExecutor sends the conversation and the tool schemas to Claude, parses the tool_use blocks in the reply, routes each call through the permission gate and feeds the results back until the task is done. ConversationMemory is thread-safe and persists recent messages to memory.json in the runtime directory from Step 3. The agent package barrel re-exports these pieces as one public API.
tour.languageLesson: A tool-use agent loop is a plain while-loop. The program calls the model, runs any requested tools, appends their results as new messages, and repeats until the model returns a final answer with no tool calls.

tour.title: Tools: Desktop Automation
tour.description: tools.py holds the tool registry and every automation handler the executor can call: files, terminal, apps, windows, web fetch with an SSRF guard, system controls, YouTube, PDF and Telegram. Tool.run strips every key that starts with '_' from the model's input, so the model cannot forge approval (audit S3). Commands are run without shell=True (audit S7).

tour.title: Permission Tiers and Approvals
tour.description: Before any tool from Step 6 runs, the permission gate puts it in one of three tiers. SAFE tools run automatically. CONDITIONAL tools get a check on every call, with no blanket allow. DANGEROUS tools always require approval (audit S4). When approval is needed, the non-blocking ApprovalManager creates a request with an unguessable id. Each request is bound to a SHA-256 hash of the call's arguments, can be used once and expires (audit S5). It can be resolved only from the HUD or Telegram, never by voice.

tour.title: Flask HUD Server
tour.description: ui_server.py runs the local Flask server on 127.0.0.1:5000, with 5001 as a fallback. It serves the ui/ assets and a JSON API (/status, /command, /approvals, /approve and more). It enforces audit S1: a per-launch token injected into the page, strict Host and Origin checks, and JSON-only state-changing requests. hud_status.py holds the live assistant state, a log ring and CPU/RAM metrics in memory, and flushes them atomically to status.json.
tour.languageLesson: An atomic file write saves data to a temporary file in the same directory and then calls os.replace() to swap it in. A reader then sees either the old file or the new one, never a half-written file.

tour.title: The Radar HUD Front End
tour.description: This is the browser side of the server from Step 8. index.html lays out the clock, system stats, command bar, approvals panel and chat feed, and carries the __HUD_TOKEN__ placeholder that the server fills in. app.js polls /status and /approvals every second, renders pending approvals with approve and deny actions, and sends commands. style.css defines the cyan-glow sci-fi radar look.
tour.languageLesson: Polling with setInterval and fetch() is a simple alternative to WebSockets for a local dashboard. Each request sends a custom header such as X-HUD-Token, and the server checks it before answering.

tour.title: Always-On Voice
tour.description: voice_service.py is the hands-free channel that main.py starts on its own thread. It covers wake-word parsing, voice activity detection (VAD), faster-whisper speech-to-text, and a TTSManager for edge-tts or Piper playback. signals.py provides a Qt-free CallbackSignal descriptor, so these listeners can offer Qt-style connect and emit without importing PySide6. Following Step 7, voice can issue commands but can never approve a dangerous action.
tour.languageLesson: A Python descriptor that implements __get__ can return per-instance state. That lets a class-level declaration like `on_text = CallbackSignal()` give every object its own callback list.

tour.title: Telegram Remote Control
tour.description: telegram_service.py gives remote access to the assistant. It includes message chunking and send helpers for text, documents and photos, a minimal Bot API client, and TelegramRemoteListener for incoming commands. TelegramApprovalBridge is the second out-of-band approval path from Step 7: it posts inline-keyboard approve and deny buttons that work only for the configured owner chat and user.

tour.title: SQLite Persistence
tour.description: db.py is the SQLite storage layer. It defines settings, conversations, messages, tool_executions and permissions tables, with dataclass row models and CRUD methods, and main.py opens it at startup. database.py is a deprecated shim that subclasses this Database so older imports keep working.
tour.languageLesson: Python dataclasses work well as lightweight row models. The database layer maps each sqlite3 row to a typed object, so the rest of the code does not pass raw tuples around.

tour.title: Windows and Proxy Helpers
tour.description: These are two specialized services that main.py reaches through the services barrel. desktop_icon_service.py uses Win32 ctypes to find Explorer's desktop SysListView32, read icon names and positions through cross-process memory, and move icons. omniroute_manager.py manages a local OmniRoute proxy on localhost:20128: it probes the proxy and starts the launcher without a shell if the proxy is down.

tour.title: Dependencies, Tests and Packaging
tour.description: requirements.txt lists the full dependency stack: the Flask HUD, the voice libraries (faster-whisper, webrtcvad, edge-tts) and the desktop automation packages. pytest.ini limits test collection to tests/ and test_agent.py, which excludes the legacy manual GUI scripts, and disables the cache provider so no .pytest_cache folder lands in OneDrive. build_exe.py uses PyInstaller to bundle main.py, the Flask HUD and the ui/ assets into a Windows console executable.

tour.title: Legacy PySide6 UI
tour.description: src/app.py and src/ui/ are the older, deprecated PySide6 interface: a 'dynamic island' chat window, a settings dialog and a system tray icon. They are kept only so old imports keep working. They wire up the same executor and services you have already seen, which shows how cleanly the headless main.py design replaced them. The root memory.py is a similar compatibility shim that only re-exports ConversationMemory. Do not extend any of these files.
